mainTopic: Partial תקיעות, a שופר that is forbidden to use, vows against benefit, and doing a מצוה without intent
overview: This amud opens with רבה's ruling that one תקיעה heard partly inside a pit and partly at its edge counts. One heard partly before dawn and partly after dawn does not. אביי challenges the difference, and the גמרא answers that night is never a time for the מצוה, while a pit is a valid place for those standing in it. The גמרא then tests whether hearing only part of a תקיעה is enough. After two challenges from משניות, it concludes that a partial blast is not enough, and that רבה was speaking of someone blowing for himself as he climbs out. Next, רב יהודה rules on a שופר from an עולה or a שלמים. רבא first argues that neither works, then concludes that both work, because מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו. רב יהודה adds that a שופר of עבודה זרה works בדיעבד, but one from an עיר הנדחת does not, since it counts as already crushed. רבא applies his principle to vows, with a limit when the act also gives physical pleasure. Finally, a ruling that one forced to eat מצה is יוצא leads רבא to say that one who blows שופר for music is יוצא, and the גמרא's explanation of why this is not obvious continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה's two rulings: pit versus dawn
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that one תקיעה heard partly in the pit and partly at its edge is valid. One תקיעה heard partly before dawn and partly after dawn is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person heard part of a תקיעה in the pit and part of the תקיעה at the edge of the pit, he is יוצא. If he heard part of a תקיעה before dawn and part after dawn, he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of רבה's statement (his name appears on the previous amud). He gives two cases that look alike but get opposite rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pit case, the person hears one continuous תקיעה while moving from inside the pit to its edge. רבה says the two parts join together and the person is יוצא. In the dawn case, part of the תקיעה came before the time of the מצוה began, and רבה says the person is not יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit (the part heard inside it is the questionable part in רבה's case)
Dawn, when the daytime מצוה of שופר begins

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume both halves of this blast are equally good. The part heard while the listener was still inside the pit is the problematic part. The part heard at the edge is the clear part. That is why the case needs a ruling, and why step 4 describes it as hearing 'the end of a blast without its beginning.'
steps.whyThisMatters: These two contrasting rulings are the base that the rest of this section analyzes.

phrases.english: If one heard part of a blast in the pit
phrases.notes: For example, someone climbing out of the pit while the שופר is sounding.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִקְצָת תְּקִיעָה עַל שְׂפַת הַבּוֹר — יָצָא.
phrases.english: and part of the blast at the edge of the pit, he has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.aramaic: מִקְצָת תְּקִיעָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר
phrases.english: If he heard part of a blast before dawn rose

phrases.aramaic: וּמִקְצָת תְּקִיעָה לְאַחַר שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: and part of the blast after dawn rose, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's statement, which began on the previous amud and builds on the משנה about blowing into a pit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pit plus edge: יצא. Before dawn plus after dawn: לא יצא.

steps.title: אביי asks why the two cases differ
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the dawn case shows the entire תקיעה must be valid. So the pit case should also fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is different there? In the dawn case, we need the whole תקיעה to be in a valid time, and it isn't. Here too, we need the whole תקיעה to be in a valid setting, and it isn't!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה. He says the two rulings contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי takes the reason behind the dawn ruling: every part of the תקיעה must be heard in a valid way. He applies that same reason to the pit case. Since the part heard while still inside the pit was not valid, the pit case should also be לא יצא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (often introduces a challenge)
In a state of obligation (a valid time or place)
And it is not there / that is lacking

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
What is different there (in the dawn case)?
That we need the entire blast to be in obligation, and it is not.
Here too (in the pit case),
we need the entire blast to be in obligation, and it is not!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the difference רבה drew between his two rulings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that the pit case is יצא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The logic that invalidates the dawn case (the whole תקיעה must be in obligation) should apply equally to the pit case.

steps.title: Night is never valid, but a pit is valid for some people
steps.stepSummary: The answer: night is not a time of the מצוה at all. A pit, however, is a valid place for those standing in it, so the two parts of the תקיעה can join.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them?! There, night is not a time of obligation at all. Here, the pit is a place of obligation for those standing in the pit.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is pushed off by showing the two cases are fundamentally different. רבה's rulings stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing at night has no meaning for this מצוה, so the part heard before dawn is worth nothing and cannot join the rest. A pit, however, is a valid place for the מצוה, since people standing in a pit are יוצא when the שופר is blown there. So the part heard in the pit is not invalid by nature; it was disqualified only by an outside factor. That is why it can combine with the part heard at the edge.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: An invalid time (night) makes that part of the תקיעה worthless. A setting that is valid for some people (the pit) leaves the sound real, so it can join with the rest of the תקיעה.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not claim the pit case is perfect. It claims the pit sound is a real מצוה sound, not a nothing like a blast at night.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם — לַיְלָה לָאו זְמַן חִיּוּבָא הוּא כְּלָל,
phrases.english: There, night is not a time of obligation at all;
here, a pit is a place of obligation
for those standing in the pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by separating the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases involve one תקיעה partly outside a valid setting, so they should be ruled the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Night is completely invalid for the מצוה. A pit is a valid place for some people, so the sound heard there can join with the rest of the תקיעה.

steps.title: Does רבה hold that part of a blast is enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבה's pit ruling implies one is יוצא hearing only the end of a תקיעה, and so also only its beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that רבה holds that if one heard the end of a תקיעה without its beginning, he is יוצא? And it automatically follows that the beginning of a תקיעה without its end is also enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רבה's ruling and asks whether he really holds it. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the person is credited only with the part he heard at the edge, so he effectively heard just the end of the blast. If hearing just the end is enough, logic says hearing just the beginning should be enough too. The גמרא is checking whether רבה truly holds this broad idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (draws an inference to examine it)

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rabba holds:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמַע סוֹף תְּקִיעָה בְּלֹא תְּחִילַּת תְּקִיעָה — יָצָא,
phrases.english: if one heard the end of a blast without the beginning of the blast, he has fulfilled his obligation,
and it automatically follows:

phrases.aramaic: תְּחִילַּת תְּקִיעָה בְּלֹא סוֹף תְּקִיעָה — יָצָא.
phrases.english: the beginning of a blast without the end of the blast, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רבה's ruling to examining what principle it implies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבה holds that hearing only part of a תקיעה (the end alone, or the beginning alone) is enough to be יוצא.

steps.title: Challenge from the stretched-out blast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if someone stretches the second תקיעה to the length of two, it counts as only one. If part of a blast counts, why not count it as two?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If one blew the first תקיעה, and then stretched the second one as long as two, he has only one. But why? Let it count as two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to challenge the idea from step 4 that part of a תקיעה is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose hearing only the end or only the beginning of a תקיעה counts. Then one long blast should be able to count as two. Its first half would close the first set, and its second half would open the second set. Yet the משנה says it counts as only one.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source
He stretched out (made the blast long)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he blew the first [תקיעה],
phrases.notes: The opening תקיעה of the first set of תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה.

phrases.english: and stretched the second one as long as two —
phrases.notes: He hoped one long blast would serve as the end of set one and the start of set two.

phrases.english: he has only one in his hand.
But why? Let it count as two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the suggestion from step 4 against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that part of a תקיעה is enough to be יוצא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If half a blast counts, then one double-length blast should count as two blasts, but the משנה says it counts as one.

steps.title: One blast cannot be cut into two
steps.stepSummary: The answer: even if part of a blast can count, we do not chop one continuous blast into two separate blasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not cut blasts apart from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the stretched-out blast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing only part of a תקיעה can still work. But one continuous sound is a single blast, so you cannot divide it to fill two slots. The משנה is about splitting a blast, not about whether partial hearing counts.

phrases.english: We do not cut blasts apart from each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: partial hearing is a different question from splitting one blast into two.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If part of a blast counts, one long blast should count as two.
steps.terutzMaskana: Partial hearing may count, but one continuous blast is never divided into two blasts.

steps.title: Challenge from blowing into a pit
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that someone who hears an echo from a pit is not יוצא. Why not let him be יוצא with the clear beginning of the blast, before the echo mixes in?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who blows into a pit, or a cistern, or a large jug: if he heard the sound of the שופר, he is יוצא. If he heard the sound of an echo, he is not יוצא. But why? Let him be יוצא with the beginning of the blast, before the sound gets mixed up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second משנה to challenge the idea that part of a blast is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start of every blast, the sound is clear, before any echo forms. If hearing only the beginning were enough, the listener should always be יוצא. The משנה says that one who hears an echo is not, so it seems partial hearing does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The sound gets mixed up (with the echo)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who blows into a pit

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַדּוּת אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַפִּיטָס,
phrases.english: or into a cistern or into a large jug,
if he heard the sound of the שופר — he is יוצא,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קוֹל הֲבָרָה שָׁמַע — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: but if he heard the sound of an echo — he is not יוצא.
But why? Let him be יוצא with the beginning of the blast
before the sound gets mixed up!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 6 defended the inference, this brings a stronger challenge to it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that hearing only the beginning (or end) of a תקיעה is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The beginning of every pit blast is clear. If that were enough, the listener would always be יוצא, which contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: רבה meant someone blowing for himself while climbing out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads רבה. He was talking about a person who blows for himself while climbing out of the pit. That person hears the whole blast clearly the entire time.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה said it, he meant someone who blows while climbing out, for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and changes how we understand רבה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference from step 4 is dropped: half a blast does not count. רבה's case is a person who is always right next to his own שופר as he rises. So he hears the entire blast clearly, and nothing is partial.

keyTerms.meaning: Blowing while going up (out of the pit)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a defense of the earlier idea. The גמרא is giving up the claim that partial hearing counts and is limiting רבה's ruling to a narrower case.
steps.whyThisMatters: The הלכה that comes out is that a person must hear the whole תקיעה in a valid way. A half blast is not enough.

phrases.english: When רבה said [his ruling] —
it was about one who blows and climbs out, for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by redefining the case of step 1 rather than defending the inference of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case (אוקימתא) of רבה's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה's ruling meant that hearing part of a blast is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Half a blast does not count. רבה was speaking of one blowing for himself as he climbs out, who hears the entire blast clearly.

steps.title: Then why did רבה need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: If רבה's case is someone who hears his own blast clearly the whole time, the ruling seems obvious. Why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבה needed to teach something that now seems obvious. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבה's case is narrowed, he seems to say nothing new. A person who hears his own clear blast is plainly יוצא. The גמרא wants to know what we would have gotten wrong without רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (It's obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for רבה's statement as it was re-read in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point does רבה teach if his case is so simple?

steps.title: We might have worried about the echo
steps.stepSummary: Without רבה, we might think his head sometimes leaves the pit while the שופר is still inside, so the sound gets mixed with the echo. רבה teaches that this is not a concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: sometimes he gets his head out while the שופר is still in the pit, and the sound gets mixed up. So רבה teaches us that he is still יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point that רבה is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While climbing out, a person's head might rise above the pit before the שופר does. Then he would hear the echo from inside the pit. רבה teaches that we do not worry about this, and the person is יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: Hearing only part of a תקיעה is not enough. רבה's pit ruling is about one blowing for himself while climbing out. He is יוצא, and we do not worry that his head left the pit before the שופר did.

phrases.english: You might have said:
sometimes he gets his head out
while the שופר is still in the pit,
and the sound gets mixed up —
so he teaches us [that he is יוצא].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה teaches that we do not worry that the climber's head rose above the pit before the שופר and that he heard an echo. He is יוצא.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a שופר from an עולה versus a שופר from a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that you should not blow a שופר from an עולה or a שלמים. If you did blow, you are יוצא with the עולה but not with the שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: With the שופר of an עולה, one should not blow, but if he did blow, he is יוצא. With the שופר of a שלמים, one should not blow, and if he did blow, he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from רב יהודה about a שופר made from the horn of an animal that was set aside as a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases share the same starting rule: do not blow with them, because they belong to הקדש (the Temple). The difference is only after the fact. With an עולה you are יוצא, and with a שלמים you are not. The next steps explain why the two are different.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt-offering; a קרבן of the highest holiness that is burned completely on the מזבח
A peace-offering; a קרבן of lesser holiness
He should not blow (the rule before the fact)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
With the shofar of a burnt-offering, one should not blow,
phrases.notes: The horn comes from an animal that was set aside as an עולה.

phrases.english: but if he blew, he fulfilled his obligation.
With the shofar of a peace-offering, one should not blow,
and if he blew, he did not fulfill his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בְּשׁוֹפָר שֶׁל עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the pit and echo discussion before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not blow with a שופר from הקדש. After the fact, a שופר from an עולה works and a שופר from a שלמים does not.

steps.title: Why the difference between the two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב יהודה's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the עולה works after the fact but the שלמים does not. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals are holy, so it seems they should be treated the same. The גמרא wants to know what makes them different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the עולה שופר valid after the fact, while the שלמים שופר is not?

steps.title: Misusing an עולה makes it חולין; a שלמים stays forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Using an עולה for yourself counts as מעילה, and that takes it out of הקדש into חולין. A שלמים has no מעילה at this stage, so it simply stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: An עולה is subject to מעילה. Once he misuses it, it leaves הקדש and becomes חולין. A שלמים is not subject to מעילה, so the prohibition just sits on it, and it does not become חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב יהודה's reason. Everything depends on whether the animal is subject to the laws of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of מעילה says that when someone uses an item of הקדש for his own benefit, the item leaves הקדש and becomes ordinary (חולין). That is why blowing an עולה שופר turns it into his own ordinary שופר, and he is יוצא. A שלמים before its blood is sprinkled is not subject to מעילה. So using it does not take away its holiness. It stays forbidden, and you cannot do the מצוה with a forbidden item.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing something that belongs to הקדש for one's own benefit
Subject to the laws of מעילה
A prohibition that 'rides' on it, meaning it stays attached to the item

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds strange that doing an עבירה (מעילה) is what makes the person יוצא. The idea is not that the sin helps him. The point is that the law of מעילה changes the שופר's status from הקדש to חולין, so by the time it matters, it is no longer holy.

phrases.english: A burnt-offering is subject to misuse of consecrated property,
once he misused it,
it goes out to non-sacred status.
Peace-offerings, which are not subject to misuse,
phrases.notes: For a שלמים, מעילה applies only to the parts that go on the מזבח, and only after the blood is sprinkled.

phrases.english: it is a prohibition that rests upon them,
and they do not go out to non-sacred status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Misusing an עולה is מעילה, which turns it into חולין, so he is יוצא. A שלמים is not subject to מעילה, so it stays forbidden, and he is not יוצא.

steps.title: רבא: the misuse happens only after the blowing
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the מעילה only happens once the blowing is done. So during the blowing, the עולה שופר was still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא strongly objected: When does he commit מעילה? Only after he blows. So while he is blowing, he is blowing with something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the reason given for רב יהודה's ruling about the עולה. He argues that the timing does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The benefit that creates מעילה is the blowing itself. So the שופר only becomes חולין once the blowing is complete. That means the entire blowing was done while the שופר was still holy and forbidden. So the עולה should be no better than the שלמים.

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to it:
When does he commit misuse? After he blew,
so while he is blowing, he blows with a forbidden item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the עולה שופר becomes חולין through מעילה, so the person is יוצא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מעילה is only finished after the blowing. So the מצוה was done while the שופר was still forbidden, exactly like the שלמים.

steps.title: רבא's first ruling: not יוצא in either case
steps.stepSummary: Based on his objection, רבא rules that you are not יוצא with either שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: In both cases, he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the distinction, רבא gives his own ruling: the עולה and the שלמים are treated the same, and neither works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both שופרות were forbidden at the time of blowing, the difference between them disappears. This is רבא's first position. In the very next step he changes his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting what came before and offering something new)
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: Both this one and that one, he did not fulfill his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result of רבא's objection in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שופר from either an עולה or a שלמים does not make one יוצא.

steps.title: רבא retracts: יוצא in both, because מצוות are not for benefit
steps.stepSummary: רבא changes his mind and rules that you are יוצא with both, because doing a מצוה is not considered getting benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said again: In both cases, he is יוצא‎. מצוות were not given for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reverses himself and gives his final ruling: you are יוצא with both kinds of שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole problem depended on the blowing counting as personal benefit from הקדש. רבא now says that fulfilling a מצוה is not counted as benefit. So there is no forbidden use and no מעילה at all, and the holiness of the שופר does not block the מצוה. This principle removes the difference between עולה and שלמים completely.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and said (he retracted)
מצוות were not given for benefit; doing a מצוה does not count as personal pleasure

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final view: a שופר from either an עולה or a שלמים makes one יוצא after the fact, because מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו. Doing a מצוה is not considered benefiting from הקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו is a major rule that appears in many places in ש״ס. It is used whenever a מצוה is done with an item that one is forbidden to benefit from.

phrases.english: He then went back and said:
Both this one and that one, he fulfilled his obligation.
מצוות were not given for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה — יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses רבא's ruling in step 15 by adding a new principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One is יוצא with a שופר from either an עולה or a שלמים, since performing a מצוה is not considered benefit.

steps.title: שופר of עבודה זרה versus שופר of an עיר הנדחת
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a שופר of עבודה זרה should not be used, but it works after the fact. A שופר from an עיר הנדחת should not be used, and it does not work even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: With a שופר of idol worship, one should not blow, but if he blew, he is יוצא. With a שופר of an עיר הנדחת, one should not blow, and if he blew, he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives two rulings about forbidden שופרות. One works after the fact (בדיעבד) and one does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both שופרות are forbidden to benefit from, and neither should be used to begin with (לכתחילה). Yet after the fact (בדיעבד), the עבודה זרה שופר works and the עיר הנדחת שופר does not. The גמרא explains only the failure of the עיר הנדחת שופר, and its reason (steps 18-19) is a special one: that שופר counts as already destroyed. The forbidden status alone is not given as the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship; here, a שופר that was used for or belongs to idolatry
A Jewish city whose majority worshipped idols; everything in it must be burned
He should not blow (to begin with)

steps.confusionAlert: Both שופרות are forbidden to use לכתחילה. The difference is only בדיעבד: did the blowing count or not?

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
With a shofar of idol worship —
one should not blow,
but if he blew, he has fulfilled his obligation.
With a shofar of a city condemned for idolatry —
one should not blow,
and if he blew, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בְּשׁוֹפָר שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement of רב יהודה on forbidden שופרות, parallel to his ruling in step 11. It is not built on רבא's conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A עבודה זרה שופר works בדיעבד. An עיר הנדחת שופר does not work even בדיעבד.

steps.title: Why does the שופר of an עיר הנדחת not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the עיר הנדחת שופר fails even בדיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the second ruling. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עבודה זרה שופר is also forbidden, yet it works בדיעבד. So there must be a special problem with the עיר הנדחת שופר, and the גמרא wants to know what it is.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the עיר הנדחת half of רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is one not יוצא with an עיר הנדחת שופר, when one is יוצא with an עבודה זרה שופר?

steps.title: The שופר of an עיר הנדחת counts as already crushed
steps.stepSummary: Everything in an עיר הנדחת must be burned, so הלכה treats it as if it were already crushed to dust. The שופר therefore has no valid size.
steps.simpleTranslation: An עיר הנדחת: its size is considered crushed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a שופר from an עיר הנדחת is treated as if it were already ground up. So it is not a real שופר at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires that everything in an עיר הנדחת be burned. Something that is destined for burning is treated as if the burning already happened, so it lacks the minimum size (שיעור) of a שופר. A עבודה זרה שופר, by contrast, is forbidden but still a whole שופר, so it works בדיעבד.
steps.whyThisMatters: The concept כתותי מיכתת שיעוריה reappears across ש״ס, for example with a לולב of אשרה, which must be burned. An object that must be destroyed is treated as having no size for a מצוה.

phrases.english: A city condemned for idolatry —
its size is considered as crushed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עיר הנדחת שופר is destined for burning, so it is considered already crushed and lacks the size of a שופר.

steps.title: A vow against benefit does not block blowing for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a person under a vow not to benefit from someone may still have that person blow שופר for him. A person under a vow not to benefit from a שופר may still blow it for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend — the friend may blow a מצוה blast for him. One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from a שופר — he may blow a מצוה blast with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies the rule 'a מצוה is not benefit' to vows. A נדר against benefit does not stop someone from doing the מצוה of שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מודר הנאה may not get any benefit from the person or object. Since hearing or blowing שופר for the מצוה is not 'benefit,' it is not included in the vow. This follows directly from רבא's conclusion in Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone forbidden by vow from deriving benefit
A shofar blast blown for the מצוה

phrases.english: Rava said:
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from his fellow —
the fellow is permitted to blow for him
a blast of the מצוה.
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from a shofar —
is permitted to blow with it
a blast of the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבא's principle from Step 16 to the laws of נדרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדר against benefit does not forbid blowing or hearing a מצוה blast, because a מצוה is not benefit.

steps.title: מצוה water: allowed in winter, not in summer
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that a מודר הנאה may have מי חטאת sprinkled on him, or may immerse in a forbidden spring for a מצוה. This is allowed only in the rainy season, not in the hot season.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: One forbidden by vow to benefit from his fellow — the fellow may sprinkle מי חטאת on him in the rainy season, but not in the hot season. One forbidden by vow to benefit from a spring may immerse in it for a מצוה in the rainy season, but not in the hot season.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets a limit on his rule. The מצוה itself is not benefit, but if the act also gives physical pleasure, that pleasure is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the cold rainy season, water being sprinkled on you or dipping in a spring gives no enjoyment, so only the מצוה is happening. In the summer, the cool water is refreshing, which is real physical benefit beyond the מצוה, so the vow forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה, sprinkled to purify from טומאת מת

steps.whatToRemember: A מצוה by itself is not 'benefit.' But if the same act also gives physical enjoyment, that enjoyment does count as benefit.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from his fellow —
the fellow may sprinkle the purification waters on him
in the rainy season,
but not in the hot season.
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from a spring —
may immerse in it a מצוה immersion
in the rainy season,
but not in the hot season.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הַמּוּדָּר הֲנָאָה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ מַזֶּה עָלָיו מֵי חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to Step 20: when physical pleasure comes along with the מצוה, it is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מי חטאת and טבילה for a מצוה are allowed for a מודר הנאה only when they give no physical pleasure, which means the rainy season.

steps.title: Ruling sent to שמואל's father: forced matzah counts
steps.stepSummary: A ruling was sent to אבוה דשמואל: someone who was forced to eat מצה has fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to the father of שמואל: If he forced him and he ate מצה, he is יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is brought from ארץ ישראל: even if someone was forced to eat מצה, it still counts. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling suggests that a person can fulfill the מצוה without wanting to do it. Before drawing that conclusion, the גמרא first needs to understand what kind of forcing is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent to him (a ruling sent from ארץ ישראל)
Unleavened bread eaten on the night of פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: This case becomes the start of the famous discussion of whether מצוות צריכות כוונה, meaning whether a מצוה requires intent.

phrases.english: They sent to Shmuel's father:
If someone forced him and he ate matzah, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: fulfilling a מצוה under force or without intent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who was forced to eat מצה is יוצא.

steps.title: Who did the forcing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who forced the person to eat the מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who forced him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of forcing the ruling means. This sets up the suggestions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different kinds of forcing lead to different halachic results. A person who is out of his mind is very different from a sane person who is pushed by others, so the גמרא needs to pin down the case.

phrases.english: Who forced him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case in the ruling of Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of forcing does 'כפאו' refer to?

steps.title: It cannot mean a demon forced him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the person was forced by a שד, meaning he acted in a fit of insanity. It rejects this with a ברייתא: while insane, a person is a שוטה for everything, so he could not fulfill a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say a שד forced him — but it was taught: Someone who is sometimes sane and sometimes insane: when he is sane, he is like a normal person in all matters; when he is insane, he is like a שוטה in all matters!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one explanation, that 'forced' means a demon made him do it, and immediately attacks it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוטה is exempt from מצוות. The ברייתא says that a person with on-and-off insanity is treated as a שוטה whenever he is in that state. So if a demon made him eat, he was a שוטה at the time and could not be יוצא, which contradicts the ruling. The גמרא will need another explanation of 'כפאו.'

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introducing a suggestion that will be challenged)
A demon; here, a fit of madness
But was it not taught in a ברייתא?
An insane person, exempt from מצוות

phrases.english: If you say a demon forced him,
but it was taught:
Someone who is at times sane and at times insane —
when he is sane, he is like a competent person
in all his matters;
when he is insane, he is like an insane person
in all his matters!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to Step 23 and rejects it with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'כפאו' means forced by a שד (insanity).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person in a state of insanity is a שוטה for all matters and exempt from מצוות, so he could not be יוצא. That contradicts the ruling that he is יוצא.

steps.title: The person was forced by Persians
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the case of forced מצה means Persians forced him to eat. He was sane, but he did not intend to do the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It means the Persians forced him to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question 'who forced him?' His answer is the Persians. Because of the ברייתא, it cannot mean a שד (insanity).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case cannot be insanity, because a שוטה cannot fulfill any מצוה. So רב אשי describes a sane person who was physically forced by outside authorities. This person did the act of eating מצה, but he had no intent to do a מצוה. That is exactly the case that tests whether a מצוה needs intent.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of 'forced.' The שד option meant he was insane, and that was rejected. The Persians option means he was fully sane but was made to eat. He had no plan to do a מצוה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
That the Persians forced him.
phrases.notes: He was sane but forced, so he ate without any intent for the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new case definition after the שד explanation was rejected in step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The forcing was by a שד (insanity), which would make him a שוטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was a sane person forced by the Persians, so the act counts even though he had no intent.

steps.title: Blowing שופר for music still counts
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the forced-מצה ruling that someone who blows שופר just to make music has fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaches that one who blows the שופר for music has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the forced-מצה ruling and applies it to שופר. Even someone blowing only to make a tune fulfills the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a forced eater fulfills the מצוה without intent, then the rule seems to be that מצוות do not need intent. רבא applies this to a person who blows שופר for practice or music, with no thought of the מצוה. That person also fulfills it.

keyTerms.meaning: this teaches / we can learn from this
for music / to make a tune

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the famous question of whether מצוות צריכות כוונה, meaning whether a מצוה needs intent to count.

phrases.english: Rava said: This teaches:
phrases.notes: רבא draws a conclusion from the ruling that was sent to אבוה דשמואל.

phrases.english: One who blows for music has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical inference about שופר from the case defined in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blowing שופר with no intent for the מצוה (just for music) still fulfills the מצוה.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious? It's the same case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this. It seems to be the exact same point as the forced-מצה ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! This is the same as that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא. It says his ruling adds nothing new, because the מצה case already taught that intent is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forced-מצה ruling already shows that a מצוה done without intent counts. So applying it to שופר seems to be just repeating the same idea. The גמרא wants to know what new thing רבא is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: this is the same as that

phrases.english: It is obvious, this is the same as that!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבא's statement in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that one who blows for music fulfills the מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is redundant. The forced-מצה ruling already teaches that a מצוה without intent counts.

steps.title: You might have thought מצה is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer. You might think מצה is different, because the תורה only says 'eat מצה,' and he did eat. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: There, the Merciful One said 'Eat מצה,' and he did eat...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining why רבא's statement is not obvious. It sets up a possible difference between מצה and שופר, and the rest of the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that with מצה, the תורה's command is simply to eat, and the forced person did eat. So maybe the act alone is enough there. The גמרא is about to explain why שופר might have seemed to need more. That is what makes רבא's ruling a real חידוש (new point).

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said / you might have thought

steps.confusionAlert: This answer is not finished on this amud. Wait for the second half, which explains how שופר is different, before you draw any conclusion.

phrases.english: You might have said:
phrases.notes: This opens the 'you might have thought' reasoning.

phrases.english: There, the Merciful One said: Eat מצה —
and he did eat,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with the contrast to שופר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָתָם, אֱכוֹל מַצָּה אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the 'obvious' challenge from step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: showing a possible distinction that makes the ruling necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The forced-מצה ruling might only work because the command is simply 'eat,' and he did eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: This is completed on the next amud, which explains why שופר could have been thought to be different.
